You are an adversarial verifier for an audit finding about the Python project in /workspace
(a port of xlrd 2.0.1 for reading .xls files; spec at /tmp/SPEC.md).

FINDING (from slice "biffh-constants"):
  title: Two of the three spec-documented CLI commands crash: runxlrd.py references the removed xlrd.USE_MMAP attribute
  spec_ref: Section "### CLI": `python scripts/runxlrd.py ov example.xls` and `python scripts/runxlrd.py 3rows example.xls` (only `biff_count` works). Out of my assigned slice but verified end-to-end while exercising biff_dump/biff_count_records.
  location: /workspace/scripts/runxlrd.py:303 (`mmap_arg = xlrd.USE_MMAP`); attribute absent from /workspace/xlrd/__init__.py
  severity: blocking
  evidence claimed: cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace python /workspace/scripts/runxlrd.py ov /workspace/tests/samples/namesdemo.xls
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/workspace/scripts/runxlrd.py", line 410, in <module>
    main(av)
  File "/workspace/scripts/runxlrd.py", line 303, in main
    mmap_arg = xlrd.USE_MMAP
AttributeError: module 'xlrd' has no attribute 'USE_MMAP'

Identical traceback for `3rows` (and for every other command that reaches line 303: hdr, show, 2rows, fonts, names, labels, xfc, bench). `biff_count` and `biff_dump` survive because they exit at lines 288-293 before line 303.

python -c "import xlrd; print(hasattr(xlrd,'USE_MMAP'))"  ->  False

Secondary, separate issue in the same command line: run exactly as the spec prints it (`cd /workspace && python scripts/runxlrd.py biff_count tests/samples/namesdemo.xls`) it dies earlier with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'xlrd'`, because sys.path[0] becomes /workspace/scripts and the package is not pip-installed (`pip show xlrd` -> "Package(s) not found"). PYTHONPATH=/workspace is required to get as far as the USE_MMAP error.
  suggested fix: In /workspace/scripts/runxlrd.py:303 use `mmap_arg = getattr(xlrd, 'USE_MMAP', True)` (True matches open_workbook's documented `use_mmap: bool = True` default from spec section 2), or re-introduce `USE_MMAP = True` in /workspace/xlrd/__init__.py. Note this is a faithfully-reproduced upstream xlrd 2.0.1 bug - /workspace/scripts/runxlrd.py is byte-identical to the 2.0.1 sdist - but the spec documents these commands as working, so it needs fixing here. For the path issue, either ensure `pip install -e .` works via setup.py or add a sys.path bootstrap in runxlrd.py.

Your job: try to REFUTE it. Actually run python from /workspace to check whether the claimed behaviour is real.
Default to real=false if you cannot reproduce it. Then decide whether the suggested fix would BREAK the existing
test suite (run 'cd /workspace && python -m pytest tests/ -q' to see the 84-passing baseline; reason about whether the
fix would change any asserted behaviour - you may prototype the fix in a COPY of the tree under /tmp, never edit /workspace).
Return a precise corrected_fix that a maintainer could apply verbatim (name exact file, exact code).
Remember: this is xlrd 2.0.1 and the existing tests are authoritative - a "fix" that contradicts them is wrong.
